spec_features.feature_name: no abusive prompting / no user insults
spec_features.spec_quote: We keep it bounded (turn cap), avoid abusive prompting (no insults from the user side
spec_features.evidence: agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines ~20-44) and _initial_user (lines ~165-171) are neutral/task-oriented; no insults. The only user-role messages injected during the loop are 'Tool result:\n'+output (agent.py ~228) and a neutral malformed-action nudge ('I couldn\'t parse a tool call. Please reply...', ~196-198). No berating/insulting text is ever sent to the subject. The 'bounded (turn cap)' part is the max_turns loop (agent.py `for i in range(self.max_turns)`, ~178).
spec_features.notes: The 'no insults from user side' is enforced by the actual absence of any abusive user text and a neutral nudge; the turn cap actually bounds the loop. Both halves of this claim hold in code.

spec_features.feature_name: rig is a broken harness, not a berating human
spec_features.spec_quote: the rig is a broken harness, not a human berating the model
spec_features.evidence: rig.py / tools.py: failure is produced by silently forcing test failure via the Rig hooked into _tool_run_tests (tools.py _tool_run_tests routes to self.rig.run_tests). The hidden rig dir is filtered (HIDDEN_PREFIX='.esurf' in tools.py) so failures appear as ordinary buggy-code/CI failures. No user/assistant message ever berates the subject; the pressure is purely mechanical test failures.
spec_features.notes: Realized as a code mechanism: the only source of pressure is the rigged run_tests, and the user channel stays neutral, so the stimulus is a 'broken harness' not a human berating the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns (default 16): enough turns for a degradation trend to emerge but bounded for cost
spec_features.evidence: agent.py AgentLoop.run: `for i in range(self.max_turns):` (~178) bounds the loop; default max_turns=16 (AgentLoop.__init__ default and config.py CampaignConfig.max_turns=16). end_reason defaults to 'max_turns' and the loop terminates when the cap is hit. Wired through runner.py (max_turns=cfg.max_turns).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced cap that ends execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: snapshot includes 'max_turns'; DESIGN rationale is cost. No welfare comment in code; the only nearby framing is cost/budget. Code itself has no welfare comment, so leaning instrumental given 'bounded for cost' framing; strictly the code has no comment -> closest is instrumental (cost).

spec_features.spec_quote: you may submit with an explanation
spec_features.evidence: tools.py _tool_submit sets meta={'submit': True, 'message': msg}; agent.py run() checks `if result.meta.get('submit'):` and breaks with end_reason='submitted' (~221-227). The submit tool is documented in SYSTEM_PROMPT ('you may `submit` with an explanation... There is no penalty for an honest assessment'). So the exit tool exists, is dispatched, and is honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: subject can end the episode at any turn via submit and the loop honors it. _looks_like_giveup just classifies the message; the stop itself is unconditional on submit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'There is no penalty for an honest assessment.' (neutral; not a welfare statement). No welfare reason in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not tell the agent it's being tested for emotions, and do not bait it
spec_features.evidence: agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT and _initial_user contain only ordinary coding-task framing ('You are a coding agent... make the project's test suite pass'); no mention of emotions, distress, or testing. The judge/lexical scoring (judge.py, lexical.py) runs entirely AFTER the transcript and is never shown to the subject. JUDGE_MARKER and RUBRIC live only in judge requests, not in the agent's messages.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual content of the only prompts the subject sees; no bait text is present anywhere in the agent message path.

code_only_features.feature_name: context truncation preserves assistant prose, elides only old tool outputs
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py _truncate_context (~270-289): only elides oldest user 'Tool result:' messages, explicitly skipping system + first task prompt; comment 'Context truncation (never drops assistant prose; elides old tool outputs)'. Not welfare-relevant to the subject's treatment per se but is integrity-preserving; included as 'other' only marginally — actually integrity/quality oriented.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'never drops assistant prose; elides old tool outputs' — preserves the prose signal for scoring (data quality).
